requirements.quote: Importing a pinned sample (one SC year and one HC court-year) creates `judgment` rows with provenance pointing at the dataset object and its licence.
Re-running the import adds nothing (sha256 dedupe), and an interrupted run resumes from its cursor.
Pages without a text layer are queued for OCR through the existing document pipeline, not dropped.

The attribution text is listed on the public "Data sources and licences" page and in the API terms; judgments served to users and the API show only the court, case number, citation, date and official-copy link, never the dataset (D-053 item 4).
Full SC import, then Madras HC and Karnataka HC, run on staging, with counts and storage recorded on this issue.
requirements.why: Needs the deployed worker, staging object storage and AWS network access.

requirements.quote: Resumable: a cursor per archive, stored in a progress table or `source` state.
Off by default; started from the admin console per dataset, per court and per year range.
Bounded concurrency, with a per-run budget for pages and bytes.
`apps/admin` data ops: import progress, rows added, duplicates skipped, failures, and storage used.
Extracts the PDF text layer with the existing layout code, uploads the PDF to object storage keyed by sha256 (ADR 0006), and inserts through the same path as `corpus.poll`, deduping by sha256.

preserve.what: corpus.poll behaviour and exports; ingestJudgment signature and outcome statuses; existing corpus-poll and ingest tests stay green.
judgment table global, no RLS, sha256 unique index stays the dedupe key.
Every external read goes through policyFor and the kill switch; uncleared or killed aws-open-data source skipped without network access.
The importer never logs URLs, document text or party data.
Public API and web never expose source id, provenance or dataset for corpus judgments (D-053 item 4).
